docket.grounds: Three legs upheld, two corrected. UPHELD and load-bearing: the rationale ends the span on a terror pronouncement said to close on the divine-title stack. So the defect is the words 'in this span' attached to a collection-scoped count, not the digit; a ruling that the digit is wrong under every object definition omits the collection scope, and a reading that treats the count as correctly scoped ignores the field's own word. docket.challenge_claim: Item one: the span's only disclosed seam driver is a bare reintroduction of the divine-speech formula by the same speaker already carrying the oracle through the preceding span, without a disclosed addressee, scene or frame-owner change to justify treating the restart as a fresh onset. Item two: the row places a paseq at a position inside the verse in the same sentence that disclaims any position knowledge, and it assigns to Bozrah a predicate the bytes give to her cities.
docket.grounds: The items are DISTINCT -- the first is a seam-warrant sufficiency defect, the second a pair of disclosure and gloss-extent defects inside the row's prose -- and all three findings stand. Warrant: the row's observed_substrate_signals carries the speech formula alone, with no frame-owner, addressee or scene key, and the rationale discloses no such change either. The bytes agree that none is there: the same divine first person carries continuously across the seam, from the mercy clause at MT 49:11 through the verse-initial formula כִּי כֹ֣ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה (oshb:Jer.49.12, byte tier), where second-masculine-singular address to the same target resumes inside the same verse at וְאַתָּ֣ה ה֔וּא נָקֹ֖ה תִּנָּקֶ֑ה (oshb:Jer.49.12, byte tier), into the first-person oath בִ֤י נִשְׁבַּ֨עְתִּי֙ (oshb:Jer.49.13, byte tier). The third-person cup clause is an a-fortiori comparison, not a fresh addressee. Under the ruled internal-cut class a divine-speech-formula onset licenses a row seam WITH a frame-owner change; none is disclosed or present, and the SAMEKH closing MT 49:11 -- real and correctly located as this row's front seam -- is single-witness tier-3 corroboration that cannot supply it. The two neighbouring header rows each disclose an accompanying addressee shift; this one does not. This does NOT refute the boundary: a verse-initial messenger-formula restart standing immediately behind a parashah break is a tier-1 signal and may drive a seam. What it defeats is the sufficiency of the warrant AS DISCLOSED and the confidence resting on it. Paseq: the rationale places the mark later in the verse in the same sentence that says the inventory gives no position within it. The seg layer is count-only and intra-verse position is unsourceable, so the first half of the sentence asserts what the second half says cannot be known; the object itself is real (1 seg at MT 49:12, single-witness) and only the position words go. Gloss extent: the closing sentence names Bozrah as an astonishment and a perpetual waste. The bytes predicate the fourfold list of Bozrah with a singular verb, כִּֽי לְשַׁמָּ֧ה לְחֶרְפָּ֛ה לְחֹ֥רֶב וְלִקְלָלָ֖ה תִּֽהְיֶ֣ה בָצְרָ֑ה (oshb:Jer.49.13, byte tier), and reserve the perpetual-wastes phrase for her cities in a separate clause with its own plural verb and subject, וְכָל עָרֶ֥יהָ תִהְיֶ֖ינָה לְחָרְב֥וֹת עוֹלָֽם (oshb:Jer.49.13, byte tier), matching “Bozrah will become an astonishment, a reproach, a waste, and a curse. All its cities will be perpetual wastes.” (web:Jer.49.13). Both witnesses agree, so the gloss overshoots its splice. Two smaller gaps confirmed for the same pass: MT 49:13 carries the participial divine formula mid-verse at tokens 3-4, נְאֻם יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.49.13, byte tier), inside the quoted oath run and never named; and observed_substrate_signals records only the speech formula though the row argues an oath formula and a divine title as well. Both of the row's Hebrew runs reach byte tier against their cited verses, and the formula at MT 49:12 is divine-mouthed with no embedded-speech ownership question at this site.
docket.remedy: boundary_rationale: delete the words placing the paseq later in the verse, keeping the count-only disclosure; re-cut the closing gloss so its extent matches its splice -- the fourfold predicate belongs to Bozrah, the perpetual-wastes phrase to her cities in the following clause; and name the participial divine formula standing mid-verse at Jer.49.13 rather than leaving it inside an unremarked quoted run. Same field: state whatever accompanying signal actually stands at the seam beside the formula restart -- the front-seam mark is already disclosed and cannot carry it alone -- or say plainly that the restart stands without one. observed_substrate_signals: add keys for the oath formula and the divine title the row already argues, and add or withhold a frame/addressee key strictly per the bytes; it is a dependent field of any driver re-weighting, which re-opens strongest_rejected_alternative, unit_type and confidence with it. confidence: re-rate against the repaired warrant rather than leaving medium standing on a bare formula restart. Tests the cures must pass: the paseq sentence must contain no intra-verse position word; the closing gloss must be reproducible clause by clause against oshb:Jer.49.13 with the subject of each verb named; and the seam sentence must name a byte-attested signal beside the formula or concede its absence. B4-1.grounds: ARBITRATION OF THE PMARKS TENSION (inventory bytes, controlling): pmarks_Jer.json records ONE entry at that key, marks[Jer.49.19] = SAMEKH - a setumah, single-witness (WLC/OSHB), tier-3 WEAK in the Prophets. The second witness agrees, closing its quotation at the end of 49:19 and carrying “Therefore hear the counsel of Yahweh, that he has taken against Edom” (web:Jer.49.20) outside it. The drawn front edge carries nothing of the kind: oshb:Jer.49.19 opens הִ֠נֵּה כְּאַרְיֵ֞ה (byte tier), a presentative plus simile - no word-event shape, no lamed-initial or non-lamed OAN header, no koh-amar, no vocative, no imperative, and not among the classified date-candidate sites. The row's stated ground for declining the seam is byte-false: the question series terminates at 49:19's verse-final accent, so nothing runs past the verse boundary. Tier-1 evidence therefore stands at the declined edge and is wholly absent at the drawn one, and the seam belongs at Jer.49.19|Jer.49.20. FORM OF THE ADOPTION: installed as a seam MOVE, not a split. A split (Jer.49.19-Jer.49.19 plus Jer.49.20-Jer.49.22) would leave the device-less Jer.49.18|Jer.49.19 edge standing as a row seam, which is the very defect being cured, and would add a row and cascade the chunk index. The Ammon header is לִבְנֵ֣י עַמּ֗וֹן at MT 49:1 (byte tier) and that unit closes four verses later at 49:6, well before the formula in question. B4-6.docket_item: CWO-5 policy ruling: may a declared closure-classed observed_substrate_signals key name a device outside the declaring unit's own span? Enumerate the declaring rows from the frozen corpus and rule ONE scope policy.
B4-6.grounds: DETERMINISTIC ENUMERATION (swept from SP/Jer/draft_rows_combined.jsonl, 276 rows; the swept object is the observed_substrate_signals key speech_formula.neum_closure, named before any digit): 10 declaring rows - P05-002 Jer.13.12-Jer.13.14, P05-013 Jer.15.5-Jer.15.9, P07-007 Jer.21.11-Jer.21.14, P08-001 Jer.23.1-Jer.23.8, P08-002 Jer.23.9-Jer.23.15, P08-004 Jer.23.23-Jer.23.32, P09-002 Jer.25.8-Jer.25.14, P09-004 Jer.25.30-Jer.25.33, P18-007 Jer.49.23-Jer.49.27, P18-024 Jer.50.31-Jer.50.32. Six of the ten close on a verse carrying no neum token: P08-001 (MT 23:8), P08-002 (MT 23:15), P09-002 (MT 25:14), P09-004 (MT 25:33), P18-007 (MT 49:27), P18-024 (MT 50:32). The census matches the docket exactly. COUNT OBJECTS NAMED AND BOTH TESTED (E-05, and the test that corrected this ruling's own first pass): object A is the CONTIGUOUS two-word run neum-YHWH, skeleton tier, verse counts, MT keys - 162 verses, matching the inventory digit; object B is the bare neum TOKEN, skeleton substring, verse counts, MT keys - 169 verses, matching the inventory digit. Object B controls, because the key claims a token and the title-stack shapes are their own count objects. The two objects agree on which six rows fail at the close, so the consequence set is object-independent; they do NOT agree on where the support lies, and object A alone would have produced two false statements here. At MT 51:57 object A misses what object B finds, the melekh-signature stack standing between the two words. At MT 50:31 object A likewise misses the stack נְאֻם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִ֖ה צְבָא֑וֹת (oshb:Jer.50.31, byte tier), which is one of the four adonai-stack sites - so P18-024, which object A shows as having no support anywhere in its span, in fact has support at its own opening verse. WHERE THE SUPPORT ACTUALLY LIES, per consequence row (neum-token verses inside each span under object B, MT keys): P08-001 MT 23:1, 23:2, 23:4, 23:5, 23:7; P08-002 MT 23:11, 23:12; P09-002 MT 25:9 and 25:12, both mid-verse and neither closing anything, with a further token one verse OUTSIDE and before the span at MT 25:7; P09-004 MT 25:31; P18-007 MT 49:26, the tsevaot stack נְאֻ֖ם יְהוָ֥ה צְבָאֽוֹת (oshb:Jer.49.26, byte tier), standing one verse before the row's own close; P18-024 MT 50:31, its opening verse. EVERY one of the ten therefore has support somewhere in its own span, and no row's support is exclusively out-of-span. That is decisive for how the policy must be worded: a span-level test alone clears all ten and settles nothing, so the operative bar has to be the verse-level test the P09-002 cure names - present in the verse it is claimed of - which is what separates the four sound rows from the six. GROUNDS FOR THE POLICY CHOSEN. (1) The ruled treatment makes the closure formula corroboration ONLY, closing a unit where a fresh tier-1 onset follows - a mechanism that attaches to the unit's own CLOSE. A token at the opening verse, or mid-verse in the middle of a span, or before the front seam, does no closure work for the declaring unit; a token before the front seam does that work for the PREVIOUS unit. (2) observed_substrate_signals is a record of the declaring row's own observed substrate and a dependent field of its drivers; a signal that stands outside the span is not this row's substrate at all. (3) The campaign already settles the same architecture for a weaker layer: parashah keys are BARRED from the field and their corroboration is carried in prose only. Out-of-span and off-close corroboration belongs in the same place. (4) Permitting qualified out-of-span keys would leave the field un-checkable by any span-scoped validator and would multiply disclosure text without adding evidence. The out-of-span arm of the policy is stated for completeness; no consequence row in this sweep turns on it.

consequence.spec: POLICY RULED (option (i), bind-or-drop, with the P09-002 cure test as the operative bar): a closure-classed observed_substrate_signals key is valid ONLY where the device it names stands in the DECLARING UNIT'S OWN CLOSING VERSE. In-span-but-not-closing support does not license it; out-of-span support NEVER licenses it. Where the key is dropped, the device is disclosed in prose with its verse ref and tier - never re-encoded under another key. CONSEQUENCE ROWS AND THE EDIT EACH TAKES (one edit per row): P08-001 Jer.23.1-Jer.23.8, P08-002 Jer.23.9-Jer.23.15, P09-002 Jer.25.8-Jer.25.14, P09-004 Jer.25.30-Jer.25.33, P18-007 Jer.49.23-Jer.49.27, P18-024 Jer.50.31-Jer.50.32 - each DROPS speech_formula.neum_closure from observed_substrate_signals, and each adds one sentence to boundary_rationale stating that its closing verse carries no closure formula and naming what actually closes the unit; where the token stands elsewhere in the span or before the front seam, that position is named in prose with its MT ref and byte tier and is NOT re-encoded as a key. P18-024's sentence states that its only in-span token stands at its OPENING verse, oshb:Jer.50.31, in the adonai-stack shape - its own count object, four sites book-wide - and not at its close. P18-007's states that its token stands at oshb:Jer.49.26, one verse before the close, in the tsevaot stack shape. Where dropping the key leaves the row's driver set thinner, the dependent fields re-open with it: strongest_rejected_alternative, unit_type and confidence are re-checked on each of the six. ROWS UNAFFECTED (key stands unchanged, device attested in the closing verse): P05-002, P05-013, P07-007, P08-004. CURE TEST each consequence row must pass: no closure-classed key survives in observed_substrate_signals whose named device is absent from the row's closing verse under the 169-verse neum-token object (skeleton tier, MT keys); and the prose sentence names the closing verse, states the absence, and names what closes the unit instead. SWEEP SCOPE (E-18): this order is carried to execution as its OWN sweep over observed_substrate_signals in draft_rows_combined.jsonl, scoped to the single key speech_formula.neum_closure (10 declarations). It is NOT folded into any row's fix and does NOT reach the sibling closure-classed keys, which are named here with their digits for a SEPARATE sweep under the same policy: speech_formula.neum_yhwh_closure, 6 declarations, 2 consequence rows (P02-004 Jer.4.14-Jer.4.18, close MT 4:18; P02-011 Jer.5.10-Jer.5.13, close MT 5:13); divine_title.neum_yhwh_closure, 6 declarations, 0 consequence rows. The three non-neum closure-classed keys (date_frame.narrative_date_closure, narrative_frame.speech_closure_transition, narrative_frame.summary_closure, 1 declaration each) name devices the neum objects cannot test and are outside both sweeps; they need their own named object before any digit.
